subject: On‑prem VPC: egress proofing & kernel routing validation

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: On‑prem VPC: egress proofing & kernel routing validation

Hi all,

Attaching the first-pass reference diagram and an egress-proofing summary for the Acme private deployment (see attachments: vpc-egress-proofing-v1.pdf, diagram-control-data.pdf). We ran into two areas where we want explicit confirmation before the handoff to Ops:

1) Kernel routing for tenant workload egress: our proposed pattern pins tenant egress through a per-tenant SNAT on the edge gateways with iptables maps + conntrack tuning. We want to avoid any behavior that would drop KV cache traffic or impede long‑lived gRPC streams to the control plane.

2) Egress filtering and telemetry: the design restricts outbound to a small CIDR set and TLS only, with mirrored flows sent to NetGrid IDS. We need to validate that NetGrid can accept mirrored traffic at the expected peak (2.4Gbps burst) and that they won't drop packets during short IGD bursts.

Specific asks:
- Sam / NetGrid: can you confirm the mirrored flow ingress limits and any special ports/protocols we should reserve? Please attach a sample netgrid-egress-policy.yaml if available.
- Jonas / Aditya: review the conntrack / iptables knobs in section 3 of the PDF — are there concerns for large KV cache windows (200k entries)?
- Irene: any compliance requirements (SOC2/PCI) we should bake into the audit log plan before we lock the private control plane egress policy?

I'd like to get a readout and agreed checklist by EOD Wednesday so we can include items in the deployment runbook.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Kimberly — quick pass from infra:

Thanks for the diagrams, good level of detail. A few notes inline:

- Conntrack sizing: 200k entries is reasonable if we set net.netfilter.ip_conntrack_max accordingly, but we should use nftables conntrack where supported. The bigger risk is conntrack timeouts for long‑lived KV cache streams — set tcp_timeout_established to 86400 for those flows or make them exempt via conntrack helpers.

- SNAT per tenant: acceptable, but watch for SNAT port exhaustion if many ephemeral outbound connections originate from a single node. Suggest a port‑range of 32768‑61000 and monitoring alerts when ephemeral usage > 75%.

- gRPC and long streams: ensure the gateway keeps the NAT mapping on idle using keepalive probes from the client side (we should include a keepalive policy in the control plane SDK).

I don't think iptables rules will drop internal control plane state if we scope rules to FORWARD chain and use zone-based policies. I've added a short sample iptables rule set to the drive link (attached in my notes).

Action: I'll prototype a conntrack tuning script and a port‑range monitor by Tuesday EOD.

—Jonas
Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hey Kimberly / team — thanks for the callout. NetGrid can accept mirrored flows and we have tiered ingestion. A few details: 

- Mirrored flow headroom: we can sustain up to 5Gbps sustained per customer with the current ingest profile for our EU‑US pair; for single region US deployments, 3Gbps sustained is the pragmatic SLA. Bursts to 6Gbps are tolerated for up to 30s but we recommend queuing at source for very regular bursts.

- Ports/protocols: mirrored traffic is layer‑2/L3 tuples; we do not inspect encrypted payloads. For the control plane telemetry, reserve ports 443 (TLS) and 12345 (custom gRPC telemetry) in your egress allowlist. We see the 12345 port used by some control plane agents for binary telemetry — we can accept it.

- netgrid-egress-policy.yaml: attached. It includes examples for mirrored flow metadata and the ACL snippet for the 12345 port.

One note: if you plan to SNAT everything through a small number of edge gateways, please share the expected number of simultaneous outbound flows per gateway so we can advise on queueing and ingress sizing.

Sam Torres
Principal Network Engineer, NetGrid
sam.torres@netgrid.com

Quick compliance check from Security & Trust:

- SOC2: we need to ensure egress metadata is retained for at least 90 days and that any mirrored telemetry containing IP addresses is treated as system logs under our retention policy. Please add a retention stanza to the runbook and flag where PII could surface.

- Audit logging: I prepared a short checklist (attached: egress-audit-checklist.xlsx) outlining required events (SNAT mapping created/destroyed, conntrack threshold alerts, outbound ACL changes). We should also enable immutable logs for the control plane config changes and integrate with our KMS for key rotation.

- Packet sampling: avoid retaining full packet captures unless strictly needed for incident response; sampled metadata is fine and will reduce storage footprint.

Irene Choi
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
